title: Finite direct image preserves dimension-filtered base flatness
statement: Let $S,W,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $W\to S$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $h:Z\to W$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $G$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $E=h_*G$, with $E(V)=G(h^{-1}V)$ and scalars restricted along $h^\sharp$. Then $E$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, and for every scheme $T\to S$ there is a canonical isomorphism $E_T\simeq h_{T,*}G_T$, where subscripts denote fibre products and tensor pullback [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every $w\in W_T$ with image $t\in T$, $(E_T)_w$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ if and only if $(G_T)_z$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ for every $z\in h_T^{-1}(w)$; an empty fibre imposes no condition. For every $n\geq0$, it follows that $G_T$ is flat at every $z\in Z_T$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(z)\geq n$ if and only if $E_T$ is flat at every $w\in W_T$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(w)\geq n$. Flatness, residue fields and transcendence degree are [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. The same equivalence holds with these pointwise conditions tested on all etale scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism], or on one surjective etale scheme atlas, of $Z_T$ and $W_T$.

proof.text: Finite $h$ is affine by definition. Thus affine base change gives that $E=h_*G$ is quasi-coherent and identifies its pullback along $W_T\to W$ canonically with $h_{T,*}G_T$ for every $T\to S$. To check finite type, work on $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset W$ with $h^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine finite-type criterion makes $M=\Gamma(h^{-1}V,G)$ a finite $B$-module. Choose $A$-module generators $b_i$ of $B$ and $B$-module generators $m_j$ of $M$. Every element of $M$ is an $A$-linear combination of the finitely many $b_im_j$. Since $E(V)=M$, the same affine criterion proves that $E$ is of finite type.

Fix $T\to S$ and $w\in W_T$ over $t\in T$. Finite base change makes $h_T$ finite; tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence and finite type, so the previous step applies on $T$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $w$ and write $h_T^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $p\subset A$ for $w$, and $M=\Gamma(h_T^{-1}V,G_T)$. Put $C=(A\setminus p)^{-1}B$ and $N=(A\setminus p)^{-1}M$. The affine module-stalk presentation identifies $(E_T)_w$ with $A_p\otimes_A M=N$, compatibly with the action of $R\to A_p$. For a point $z$ above $w$, corresponding to $q\subset B$, it identifies $(G_T)_z$ with $M_q$, compatibly with the same base action. Here the tensor-to-fraction identification sends $(a/s)\otimes m$ to $am/s$ and $m/s$ to $(1/s)\otimes m$.

source.place: Tag 05UF, lemma-flat-dimension-n-representable, finite-direct-image paragraph; schemes.tex Tags 01HV and 01IA for stalks

proof.text: The localized algebra $C$ is finite over the local ring $A_p$: the fractions $b_i/1$ of the finite generators of $B$ still generate, by clearing the common scalar denominator. Base change of a ring localization identifies $C$ with $B\otimes_A A_p$. Every maximal ideal $Q$ of $C$ therefore contracts to $pA_p$. The localization-prime statement says that $q=Q\cap B$ is prime, disjoint from the image of $A\setminus p$, and $Q=qC$. The preimage of $Q$ in $A$ is $p$, since $Q\cap A_p=pA_p$. Thus $q$ is precisely a point $z\in h_T^{-1}(w)$. This argument needs neither a surjective map $h_T$ nor a nonempty fibre.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization; the maximal-contraction input of Tag 00GU, lemma-integral-going-up, specialized to finite algebras over A_p

proof.text: For any $q\subset B$ over $p$, all scalar denominators from $A\setminus p$ avoid $q$. Localizing $N$ further at the image of $B\setminus q$ gives $M_q$: the maps are $(m/s)/(b/1)\mapsto m/(sb)$ and $m/b\mapsto(m/1)/(b/1)$. The equivalence relation on fractions verifies these formulas are inverse and $R$-linear. If $Q$ is maximal in $C$ and $q=Q\cap B$, every element of $C\setminus Q$ is $b/s$ with $b\notin q$; inverting these is the same as inverting $b/1$, since $s/1$ is already a unit. Consequently $N_Q=M_q$ as $R$-modules as well.

source.place: Section 00CM, definition-localization-module (Tag 07JZ), fraction equivalence relation; explicit two-stage localization calculation

proof.text: If $(E_T)_w=N$ is $R$-flat, localizing this $C$-module at the image of $B\setminus q$ preserves $R$-flatness. Step 4 identifies the result with $(G_T)_z=M_q$ for every point over $w$. Conversely, if all these stalks are $R$-flat, Step 3 assigns such a point to every maximal $Q\subset C$, and Step 4 identifies $N_Q$ with its stalk. The maximal-localization flatness test gives that $N$ is $R$-flat. This also proves the empty-fibre case: there are then no maximal ideals of $C$ by Step 3, so the same test applies with a vacuous hypothesis. Thus the claimed stalk equivalence holds for every $w$.

Finite $h_T$ is integral. Its affine residue-field extensions $\kappa(w)\to\kappa(z)$ are therefore algebraic. The transcendence-degree tower formula and its algebraicity criterion give $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(z)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(w)$. Suppose $E_T$ satisfies the threshold condition and take $z$ above $w$ with degree at least $n$: the degree equality and Step 5 give flatness at $z$. Conversely, for $w$ of degree at least $n$, every point above it has the same degree and is flat by the condition on $G_T$; Step 5 gives flatness at $w$, including when that fibre is empty. This proves the threshold equivalence for every $n\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 05UF, finite-direct-image paragraph; groupoids.tex Tag 03BL, final paragraph; fields.tex Tag 030H, lemma-transcendence-degree-tower

proof.text: Finally $W_T\to T$ is locally of finite type by base change. So is $Z_T\to T$: on any affine base chart, choose a finite-type affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $W_T$; its inverse image has coordinate algebra $B$ finite as an $A$-module. A finite set of module generators of $B$, together with a finite set of algebra generators of $A$ over the base chart, generates $B$ as a base algebra. The pullbacks of $E$ and $G$ are finite-type quasi-coherent modules by Step 2. Apply the dimension-flatness chart criterion separately to $(W_T,E_T)$ and $(Z_T,G_T)$: on each, the intrinsic pointwise condition is equivalent to testing all etale scheme charts and also to testing any one surjective etale scheme atlas. Substituting these two equivalences into Step 6 gives exactly the last clause. The identity chart shows directly that no pointwise condition is lost for schemes.
